turns.question: Where is application-level route handling wired up, and is the router itself implemented inside this repository?
turns.text:
Confirmed — `lib/` contains no `router.js` or `router/` directory; only `application.js`, `express.js`, `request.js`, `response.js`, `utils.js`, `view.js`.

## Answer

**Where application-level route handling is wired up:**

- **`lib/express.js`** — `createApplication()` (line ~36) builds the `app` function, mixes in `proto` (from `lib/application.js`) and `EventEmitter`, sets up `app.request`/`app.response` prototypes, and calls `app.init()`. It also re-exports `exports.Route = Router.Route` and `exports.Router = Router` (lines ~65-66), sourced directly from the external `router` package (`var Router = require('router');`, line 19).

- **`lib/application.js`** is where the actual wiring lives:
  - `app.init()` (line 59) defines a lazily-created `router` property via `Object.defineProperty(this, 'router', ...)` (lines 68-82): on first access it does `router = new Router({ caseSensitive, strict })` — instantiating the external Router.
  - `app.handle = function handle(req, res, callback)` (line ~152) is the core dispatch entry point: it builds a `finalhandler`-based `done` callback, sets `X-Powered-By`, binds `req`/`res` circular refs and prototypes, then delegates via **`this.router.handle(req, res, done)`**.
  - `app.use` (~line 190) proxies to `this.router.use(path, fn)` (handling the "mounted sub-app" case specially).
  - `app.route = function route(path) { return this.router.route(path); }` (~line 256) proxies to `Router#route()`.
  - `app.param` proxies to `this.router.param(name, fn)` (~line 331).
  - The HTTP verb methods (`app.get`, `app.post`, etc.) are generated in a loop — `methods.forEach(function (method) { app[method] = function (path) { var route = this.route(path); route[method].apply(...); ... } })` (~line 471) — each ultimately going through `app.route()` → `this.router.route()`.
  - `app.all` (~line 494) does the same across all HTTP methods.
  - The exported `createApplication` function itself, `app = function(req, res, next) { app.handle(req, res, next); }`, is what Node's `http.createServer` invokes on each request (via `app.listen`, defined further down in `application.js`, which wraps `http.createServer(this)`).

**Is the router implemented in this repo? No.**

- `lib/application.js` line 26: `var Router = require('router');`
- `lib/express.js` line 19: `var Router = require('router');`
- `package.json` `dependencies`: `"router": "^2.2.0"` — a separate, external npm package (also by the Express org, `pillarjs/router`), not vendored or reimplemented here.
- The Express repo's `lib/` directory contains no router implementation file — only `application.js`, `express.js`, `request.js`, `response.js`, `utils.js`, `view.js`. All routing logic (path matching, layer stacks, `Route`, param handling) lives in the external `router` package; this repo only wires it up and adds the app-level convenience API (verb shortcuts, mounting, view rendering, settings, etc.).

**Not verified:** I did not fetch/inspect the actual source of the external `router` npm package (`pillarjs/router` or wherever `router@2.2.0` is published) to confirm its internal implementation — only that Express itself does not contain it and imports it as a dependency. I also did not check `test/Router.js` or `test/Route.js` contents in detail (only saw they exist), and did not inspect `lib/request.js`/`response.js`/`view.js` since they weren't relevant to the routing question.
